name: ModelGain Content Link Health Check – Broken Link Checker
author: ModelGain.com

sections.description:
Broken links frustrate readers, waste crawl budget and make a site look abandoned. Most broken link checkers either need a cloud account or flood you with “broken” results that are really rate limits, logins or bot protection.

ModelGain Content Link Health Check is a lightweight broken link checker that runs on your own WordPress site. It scans links in published posts, pages and other public post types, checks each unique URL in small batches, and shows which post uses which link, so fixing takes minutes.

Fewer false positives

  • Broken is reserved for hard not-found responses: HTTP 404 and 410.
  • Redirect highlights 3xx responses and shows the target, so you can update old URLs.
  • Retry is used for 401/403, 429 rate limits, 5xx server errors and DNS/TLS/network failures, which are often temporary or caused by bot protection.
  • OK means the URL responded successfully during the scan.

One blocked or rate-limited request is never presented as proof that a page disappeared.

Built for real sites

  • No account, no cloud crawler. Discovery, deduplication and classification run on your server.
  • Gentle on hosting. Short browser-driven batches instead of one long PHP request. Each URL is checked once even if it appears in many posts.
  • Resume scan. Close the tab mid-scan and continue where it stopped.
  • Every problem is reachable. Results open on Needs attention (Broken, Redirect, Retry and Unknown), with status filters and pagination for large sites.
  • Source evidence. Each URL lists the posts that contain it, with edit links.
  • Recheck one link after you fix it, without rescanning the whole site.
  • Read-only. It never edits posts, unlinks URLs or creates redirects behind your back.
  • Clean uninstall. Scan data lives in two small local tables that are removed on uninstall.

The plugin scans anchor (href) links stored in WordPress content. It does not crawl rendered page-builder output or check image, script or style assets.

Pro add-on: get told when links break

The free plugin is complete for manual scans and stays free, with no locked features or license prompts. If you would rather not remember to scan, the optional Pro add-on adds:

  • Scheduled daily or weekly background scans.
  • One email per scheduled scan, only when links break that were fine in the previous scan (optionally new redirects too).
  • Scan history (last 20 scans): newly broken links, new redirects and links that were fixed.
  • CSV export of the latest results with post title, view URL and edit URL.
  • WP-CLI: wp modelgain-clhc scan --fail-on=new-broken, history and export.

Pro is $19.99 per year or $29.99 once for lifetime use, per site, sold through Freemius.

External services

ModelGain Content Link Health Check sends HTTP requests only when an administrator starts a scan or manually rechecks a URL. The destination URLs come from links already stored in published WordPress content.

For each discovered HTTP/HTTPS link, the plugin first sends a HEAD request. If the destination rejects HEAD with HTTP 403 or 405, the plugin may send a bounded GET request with a Range header to obtain enough response information for diagnostics. The request uses a User-Agent containing the plugin version and this site’s public home URL. As with ordinary server-to-server HTTP traffic, the destination can observe the originating server IP address.

The plugin does not send WordPress account credentials, cookies, post contents, customer data, or a central telemetry payload. Because destinations come from links in the site’s own published content, they may belong to many unrelated third-party websites; there is no single external service operator or universal terms/privacy URL for those destinations.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New by searching for “ModelGain Content Link Health Check”, or upload the ZIP.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open Tools → Content Link Health.
  4. Click Start fresh scan and keep the browser page open while the incremental scan runs. If you close it, use Resume scan.
sections.faq:
How do I find broken links in WordPress?

Install this plugin, open Tools → Content Link Health and click Start fresh scan. When it finishes, the Needs attention view lists broken links, redirects and links to retry, each with the posts that contain it.

Does this plugin edit or unlink broken URLs?

No. The plugin is read-only. It gives you source-page evidence so you can decide what to change.

Why is a 403 or 429 response not marked Broken?

Because those codes can be caused by authentication, anti-bot rules, rate limiting, or other request-specific conditions. The plugin labels them Retry so a transient or automated-client restriction is not presented as proof that the URL is gone.

Will it slow down my site?

Checks only run while an administrator has the scan screen open, in short batches. Nothing runs on the front end and there is no background crawler in the free plugin.

Does this plugin need a cloud account?

No. Discovery, deduplication, status classification, and scan storage run on your WordPress site.

Does it follow redirects?

The first request does not automatically follow redirects because the redirect itself is useful maintenance evidence. The plugin records the redirect response and target when the server provides one.

Does it scan images and page-builder rendered output?

Not currently. The plugin scans anchor links stored in WordPress post content.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. The free plugin is complete for manual scans and will stay free. The separate Pro add-on adds scheduled scans, scan history and comparison, an email when new broken links appear, CSV export and WP-CLI commands. The small Pro card on the scan screen can be hidden with one click, and the free plugin never asks for a license.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Clearer plugin name, description and FAQ for people searching for a broken link checker.
  • A small, dismissible card on the scan screen describes the optional Pro add-on. It is hidden when Pro is active. No feature of the free plugin changed or became limited.
  • Uninstall also removes the per-user “hide Pro card” preference.

1.0.0

  • Added status filters (Needs attention, Broken, Redirects, Retry first, Unknown, OK, All) and pagination, so every result is reachable on large sites instead of only the first 100.
  • Added Resume scan to continue an interrupted scan without starting over.
  • Added stable add-on hooks: linkprobe_loaded and linkprobe_scan_completed.
  • No change to stored data, settings or the plugin slug.

0.1.1

  • Unified the public plugin name and publisher branding under ModelGain. No change to plugin slug, settings, stored data, or behavior.

0.1.0

  • Added local link discovery for published public post types.
  • Added low-resource incremental URL checking.
  • Added conservative Broken, Redirect, Retry, Unknown, and OK classifications.
  • Added source-post evidence and individual URL rechecks.
  • Added clean uninstall of local diagnostic data.
